simple.meaning: חֱמָא (chĕmâʼ) is a Hebrew word meaning “anger.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חֱמָא (H2528) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 3:13, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֱמָא (H2528) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חֱמָא (H2528) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חֱמָא (chĕmâʼ) / H2528 is traced through Daniel 3:13, Daniel 3:19 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Then Nebuchadnezzar in rage and fury commanded that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego be brought. Then these men were brought before the king.

timeline.evidenceText: Then Nebuchadnezzar in rage and fury commanded that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego be brought. Then these men were brought before the king.

Then Nebuchadnezzar was full of fury, and the form of his appearance was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He spoke, and commanded that they should heat the furnace seven times more than it was usually heated.
